The branch is a 4-file change (`c495c922f codex title fix`) that adds an injected-preamble filter so `entire session attach` doesn't title a checkpoint with Codex's instruction preamble. 12 findings above; the three that matter:

**The fix doesn't fix the bug.** I verified this directly rather than take the review's word for it. `isInjectedInstructionPrompt` matches `# AGENTS.md instructions for ` (with that trailing suffix) and `<environment_context>`. But the repo's own Codex fixture has a user-role message whose first `input_text` item is a bare `# AGENTS.md\nThese are the project instructions.` — no suffix, no match. Running `FirstDisplayPrompt` over the list `codex.ExtractPrompts` actually produces for that fixture returns the AGENTS.md block, not the real prompt. The two new tests pass only because their fixtures put `<environment_context>` first.

Worth noting: the review's own example (`<permissions instructions>` leaking) was wrong — that item is `role: developer` and `ExtractPrompts` already drops it. The leak is the bare AGENTS.md block.

**The complete prefix list already exists** at `cmd/entire/cli/transcript/compact/codex.go:280` (`isCodexSystemContent`, 6 anchored prefixes including bare `# AGENTS.md`). The diff wrote a second, narrower copy instead, and the drift between the two *is* the bug. Reusing that helper fixes the headline defect and the duplication in one move.

**The JSONL branch lost a fallback the extractor branch kept.** `attach_transcript.go:32` filters with no `else`, so a transcript whose only user content is injected now yields `FirstPrompt=""` — no `prompt.txt`, no title, and no warning either, because `warnEmptyTranscriptMetadata` bails on `TurnCount != 0`. Same for `--review`'s prompt and its warning. Line 74 has the `prompts[0]` fallback for exactly this case.

Beyond those: `TurnCount` still counts preambles as turns (a new test asserts `2` for a one-prompt session), and `ExtractFirstPrompt` in `strategy/common.go` — which feeds `checkpoint list`, `explain`, and `restoredPromptPreview`'s *first* branch — is unfiltered, so the primary title path is untouched. That last one means `restoredPromptPreview` returns early via `ExtractFirstPrompt` whenever `prompt.txt` exists, making the refactored `FirstDisplayPrompt` unreachable in the normal case.

The sessions list (e.g. [https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire.io/sessions](<https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire.io/sessions>)) shows many sessions titled literally `<environment_context>`. Every affected row is a **Codex** `agent_review` **session** (the automated trail Reviewer): verified via prod query — all of them have `"kind": "agent_review"`, `"agent": "Codex"`, and their stored `prompt` column is literally `<environment_context>`. New sessions are still affected daily (checked sessions from 2026-08-11 through 2026-08-13), so this is live, not stale data from before the <issue id="e55bb9b6-803b-4572-967d-aa27d3f330d6" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1214/session-naming-haiku-over-declines-nameable-sessions-and-returns-an">ENT-1214</issue> stripping fix (shipped 2026-07-30).

The AI-generated name is never written for these sessions; the UI falls back to a poisoned heuristic. Three defects stack up:

## Root cause chain (verified end to end)

**1. The CLI records the wrong prompt (root cause — cli repo).**
Codex emits its runtime preamble as a *separate synthetic user message* (`<environment_context>…</environment_context>`), with the real ask in a second user message. Raw transcript of session `01KZY24D1RCV6AKCB6CQ5F64VS` (repo `01KS6GKTXQW8Z1CV8CNPYRV2ZJ` = entirehq/entire.io): entry 5 is pure env-context, entry 8 is the real prompt ("Review the changes on branch…").

The Reviewer runner ingests via `entire attach --review`, and that path does `meta.FirstPrompt = prompts[0]` (`attach_transcript.go:69`, via codex `ExtractPrompts` which returns ALL user input_text messages) and records **only** that one prompt (`attachPrompts`, `attach.go:197`). Result: the checkpoint's `prompt.txt` is 355 bytes of pure env-context (verified by reading the blob from `refs/entire/checkpoints/…` for checkpoint `01KZY1WHZXSMAQ6ZFY14C974KX`); `metadata.json` has `"review_prompt": "<environment_context>…"` too.

The CLI already has exactly the right filter — `isInjectedInstructionPrompt` in `strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go:836` skips `<environment_context>`-prefixed prompts — but only the rewind/display path uses it, not attach. That's why normal Codex sessions get good titles and only review sessions break.

**2. Ingest's preview fallback resurrects the boilerplate (entire-api).**
`firstMeaningfulLine` (`internal/ingest/checkpoint.go:747`) correctly strips injected blocks, but falls back to the *literal first line* when nothing survives — storing `<environment_context>` in `sessions.prompt`. The display heuristic is `prompt → commit subject → "Untitled session"` (`buildSessionDisplayName`), so the poisoned non-empty preview **shadows a perfectly good commit subject** like "fix(search): separate unresolved agents from session details".

**3. The AI namer runs, then the model declines (entire-api / repo-activity).**
Datadog logs (service `repo-activity`) for the session above show the pipeline working as designed right up to the model: `prompt_source: git, prompt_present: false, prompt_chars: 0` (extraction correctly emptied the boilerplate), `commit_message_count: 1` — then `sessionname: model returned empty name`. The system prompt tells the model to return empty rather than invent, and "(no prompt)" + one commit message trips that. Volume: ~356 empty-name declines in a 6-hour window (prod+staging). Each decline burns a refinement attempt; once capped (`MaxNameRefinements`), the session is never renamed and the UI shows the heuristic — the poisoned preview — forever.

* **entire-api ingest (fixes display for any agent):** drop the literal-first-line fallback in `firstMeaningfulLine` — store empty and let the heuristic fall through to the commit subject.
* Optional: tune the namer prompt so a lone commit message is enough to name from — with the two fixes above this matters much less.

| `# AGENTS.md instructions for …` | 107 | yes |

**Correction to my first finding:** the bare `# AGENTS.md` shape I flagged does not occur in any real rollout — it only exists in the synthetic `codex_full.jsonl` compact fixture. The branch's two prefixes are exactly the two real dominant shapes, covering 153/164 (93%) of sessions, including the reported `<environment_context>` symptom. The fix does what ENT-1653 asked for, and its test fixtures are representative, not lucky. Drop that finding.

**The residual gap is real but different:** 11/164 (7%) still leak, via `<recommended_plugins>`, `<user_action>`, `<turn_aborted>`. `<user_action>` matters most here — its content begins *"User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model"*, i.e. it lands in exactly the `agent_review` flow the issue is about, so those sessions would be titled with a review-tool preamble instead of the ask.

**This also weakens my "just reuse `isCodexSystemContent`" recommendation.** That helper covers `<turn_aborted>` but not `<recommended_plugins>` or `<user_action>` — so reusing it fixes 1 of the 11, not all of them. The duplication finding still stands (two drifting classifiers for one concept), but consolidating on the existing list isn't sufficient; both lists need the three new prefixes, or the predicate needs to treat a first line that is a bare `<tag>` as injected.

**Finding #3 (`ExtractFirstPrompt` unfiltered) should be downgraded.** The issue explains why normal Codex sessions title fine despite it: server-side `firstMeaningfulLine` strips injected blocks, and normal sessions' `prompt.txt` holds all prompts joined, so the real one survives. Review sessions store only `prompts[0]`, so nothing survives and ingest falls back to the literal first line. So the unfiltered CLI reader affects local `checkpoint list`/`explain` output, not the production title bug — real, minor, not blocking.

**Finding #4 (TurnCount) gets stronger.** Across those rollouts there are 60 `<turn_aborted>` and 58 `<subagent_notification>` user items, all currently counted as user turns on top of the preambles.

Unchanged and still worth fixing before merge: the missing fallback on the JSONL branch (`attach_transcript.go:32`) that silently yields no title *and* no warning, and the unanchored `strings.Contains` clause that can misclassify a genuine prompt. Both are cheap.

Net: the branch correctly implements the CLI half of ENT-1653 and I'd land it after the fallback fix; the three extra prefixes are a worthwhile follow-up rather than a reason to hold it.

Done. `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` all green (0 lint issues, full unit + integration + both E2E canaries passing).

## What changed

**One classifier instead of two.** `textutil.IsInjectedPrompt` (new leaf-package helper) is now the single source of truth. `strategy.FirstDisplayPrompt` and `compact.isCodexSystemContent` both delegate to it, so the drift that caused the gap can't recur. The prefix list is the union of both old lists plus the three shapes I measured: `<recommended_plugins>`, `<user_action>`, `<subagent_notification>`, `<turn_aborted>`, `<apps_instructions>`, `<plugins_instructions>`, and bare `# AGENTS.md`.

**The `<INSTRUCTIONS>` clause is anchored, not deleted.** No user item in 164 rollouts starts with `<INSTRUCTIONS>`, so I kept the original intent but made it `HasPrefix` + `Contains` instead of two unanchored `Contains` calls. `"why does the AGENTS.md instructions block get wrapped in <INSTRUCTIONS> tags?"` now stays a prompt — there's a test for exactly that.

**The JSONL branch got its fallback**, matching the extractor branch: an all-injected transcript keeps the raw preamble as its title rather than silently producing no `prompt.txt`, no title, and no warning. The return guard gained `|| meta.FirstPrompt != ""` so it doesn't fall through to the Gemini parser.

**Turn counts exclude injected items** via a shared `countUserTurns`, applied on all three paths (JSONL, native extractor, Gemini) — previously only one path filtered anything. I corrected the two tests that asserted the inflated count.

Also: dropped the pass-through `IsInjectedInstructionPrompt` wrapper, dropped the duplicate blank `codex` import in the test file, replaced the inaccurate "same filter the rewind display path applies" comment, and documented that `FirstDisplayPrompt` doesn't truncate.

## Verification

Rather than trust fixtures, I ran the code over all 164 real Codex rollouts in `~/.codex/sessions`:

| | Sessions titled with injected content |
|---|---|
| `main` (no filter) | 164 / 164 |
| branch as committed | 12 |
| with these fixes | **4** |

The remaining 4 have no genuine user prompt anywhere in the transcript (preamble + abort, or a review-tool result only), so the fallback title is the intended behaviour — not a leak.

Two new tests: `textutil` covers every real rollout shape plus six genuine prompts that mention the markers; `TestExtractTranscriptMetadata_JSONLOnlyInjectedPreamble` covers the JSONL degenerate case that had no coverage.

I left the work uncommitted since you didn't ask me to commit. One thing worth noting: this is only the CLI defect from ENT-1653 — the ingest `firstMeaningfulLine` literal-first-line fallback and the namer decline are separate repos, and already-affected sessions still need the backfill the issue describes.
